items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 1, 2026
items.excerpt: - Golden State Valkyries beat Atlanta Dream to win first WNBA championship The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream 68-63 to win their first Women's National Basketball Association (WNBA) championship in their second season. French international Gabby Williams led Golden State with 30 points in the decisive Game 7 at Chase Center in San Francisco, helping the team secure a 4-3 victory in the best-of-seven Finals series. Williams scored 28 of her points in the second half, including a crucial 3-pointer with just over two minutes remaining that put Golden State ahead for good. Atlanta led 30-24 at halftime, but the Valkyries rallied in the third quarter, outscoring the Dream 21-14 to take a narrow lead into the final period. Kiah Stokes contributed 13 rebounds for Golden State, while Veronica Burton made two late free throws to seal the victory. The game marked the first Game 7 in WNBA Finals history, with the championship series expanded to a best-of-seven format in 2025.

items.title: Strong growth and inflation paints mixed picture of economy days before midterm elections | | midfloridanewspapers.com
items.excerpt: - By CHRISTOPHER RUGABER AP Economics Writer ... - Author email (cindy.marshall@highlandsnewssun.com) - Nov 1, 2026 - 13 hrs ago WASHINGTON — U.S. economic growth was notably strong from July to September, yet inflation accelerated at the same time, new data showed Thursday, painting a mixed picture about the country’s economy less than a week before midterm elections in which the uncomfortably high cost of living looms larger than perhaps any other issue. Strong consumer spending and soaring investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure were key drivers of growth in the third quarter. When unemployment is as low as it is right now, consumers often spend at a healthy clip and they are doing so, particularly wealthier Americans who are riding a wave of record stock market gains. Consumer spending climbed 3.8% at an annual rate, marking the second straight quarter of strong growth and far exceeding the 0.7% increase in the first three months of the year. Business investment, driven by spending on AI infrastructure, jumped 12.7%, the most in six years. How long can this economic growth continue? Yet economists worry that persistently high prices are eroding Americans’ ability to keep up. Thursday’s data suggest consumers are increasingly dipping into savings to cover their costs. After-tax incomes, adjusted for inflation, slipped from August to September and were up just 1% from a year earlier. At the same time, inflation-adjusted spending rose 2.5% from a year earlier. “High energy prices are chipping away at purchasing power,” Ksenia Bushmeneva, an economist at TD, a bank, wrote. “Real income failed to grow for a second consecutive month, while the saving rate continued to decline. Together with higher borrowing costs, these headwinds are likely to weigh on consumer demand in the coming quarters.” Inflation worsens Consumer prices rose 3.6% in September from a year earlier, the Commerce Department said Thursday, up from 3.4% in August. On a monthly basis, prices climbed 0.5%, up from 0.3% in August and the highest figure since May. Rising gas prices drove much of the inflation increase as renewed violence in the Middle East kept oil prices above $100 a barrel, up from below $70 before the Iran war. But prices also rose outside of the energy sector. The cost of services such as shipping, hotel rooms, and utilities increased rapidly from August to September, a sign that inflation is spreading and growing more entrenched. The average price of a gallon of gas in the U.S. was $4.23 on Thursday, 39% more than it cost a year ago. Diesel prices have risen much faster. While most consumers don’t buy diesel, it has an outsized impact on inflation because it is used in industrial sectors and shipping. “The inflation outlook has become more concerning,” Bushmeneva said. “Price pressures are showing signs of heating up. Elevated gasoline prices are keeping headline inflation hot, but underlying pressures are also broadening.” Polls show that rising inflation has soured most voters on the economy, leading them to give President Donald Trump poor marks for his handling of rising prices. Trump campaigned in 2024 on lowering the cost of living, including bringing the cost of gas below $2 a gallon. Excluding the volatile energy and food categories, core inflation also picked up last month. It increased 3.1% from a year ago in September, up from 3% in August, the Commerce Department said. From August to September, core prices rose 0.3%, the same as the previous month. Will rising inflation raise borrowing costs? The new economic growth and inflation numbers arrive a day after the Federal Reserve, the agency tasked with combating inflation, left its key interest rate unchanged. Yet strong economic growth and persistently higher prices could mean more pain for Americans when the Fed meets in December. The Fed is now much more likely to raise its key interest rate, which could lift borrowing costs across the economy. “If the Federal Reserve is looking for more information on why they should act to restore price stability they can find it inside a slate of robust spending, historically low jobless claims, stratospheric private non-residential investment, and sizzling inflation data,” Joe Brusuelas, chief economist at RSM, a tax advisory firm, wrote. Thursday’s inflation data come from the personal consumption expenditures price index, which typically echoes the better-known consumer price index published earlier this month. The Fed more closely monitors the PCE index because it puts less weight on housing prices and allows for changes in consumers’ shopping habits.

items.title: Fed’s preferred inflation gauge rose in September as third-quarter GDP beats expectations | The New York Ledger
items.excerpt: November 1, 2026 in News The Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge rose further away from the central bank’s target in September as consumers face price pressures. The Commerce Department on Thursday reported that the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index rose 0.5% on a monthly basis in September and was up 3.6% from a year ago. Both figures were in line with the expectations of economists polled by LSEG. Core PCE, which excludes volatile measurements of food and energy prices, was up 0.3% on a monthly basis and 3.1% year over year. Those figures were both in line with economists’ expectations. FEDERAL RESERVE MAKES INTEREST RATE DECISION AHEAD OF MIDTERMS Federal Reserve policymakers are focused on the PCE headline figure as they try to bring inflation back to their long-run target of 2%, though they view core data as a better indicator of inflation. Compared with August’s readings, headline PCE ticked up from 3.4% to 3.6%, while core PCE rose from 3% to 3.1%. Goods prices were up 3.9% year over year, while services prices increased 3.5% from a year ago in September. The personal savings rate as a percentage of disposable personal income was 3.8%, down from 4% in August. Over the last two years, the savings rate has declined from a peak of 6.2% in April 2025 and from 5.6% in January 2026. While inflation moved further away from the Fed’s 2% target, the Commerce Department also released the advance estimate for third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP), which grew more than expected. The Bureau of Economic Analysis estimated that third-quarter GDP was 3.4%, above the 3.2% estimate of economists polled by LSEG. The BEA will release two subsequent revisions of the third-quarter GDP data. ... Bret Kenwell, U.S. investment analyst at etoro, said that “today’s in-line PCE report offered little in the way of surprise. But the lack of a shock does not mean the lack of a problem: Both headline and core PCE rose to their highest levels since May, underscoring that inflation remains a stubborn issue.” ... ### What does it mean for the Fed and interest rates? The market continues to expect the Fed to hike interest rates by 25 basis points in December, which would bring the federal funds rate to a range of 4% to 4.25% once implemented. The CME FedWatch tool shows a 79.6% probability the Fed will hike by 25 basis points in December, down slightly from 84.2% yesterday but higher than the 73.3% probability a week ago.

items.title: Midterm Count, Alaska FBI Knocks, Iran's Offer | Bluebill
items.excerpt: ### Why Tuesday's Count Takes Time Nearly 50 million Americans have already voted, and almost none of those ballots have been counted. Officials can prepare early ballots, but they don't tally them until Election Day. So when polls close Tuesday, the country starts a count that some states will finish in hours and others in weeks. Start with the ballots still on kitchen tables. In Michigan, a mailed ballot must reach the clerk by 8 p.m. on Election Day, or it doesn't count. Most states, Florida included, have the same kind of deadline. The Postal Service suggests mailing a ballot at least a week early, so anyone still holding one has better odds at a drop box. And one state changed its rule this year in a way that could catch some voters off guard. Turnout is running hot. Ohio broke its midterm early-voting record Saturday, with nearly 1.5 million ballots already in. So why does counting take so long in some places? Mail ballots are slow work. Workers match each envelope's signature to voter records, then open it and flatten the ballot for scanning. Some states let that prep start weeks early. A few, including New Hampshire, don't allow it until Election Day. Then there's the calendar. California counts ballots postmarked by Election Day that arrive up to a week later. Its counties have 13 days to report most results. Alaska accepts ballots mailed from overseas for 15 days, according to PolitiFact. Alaska and Maine also use ranked-choice voting. Voters rank the candidates in order. If nobody tops 50%, the last-place finisher is dropped and those votes move to each voter's next choice. Maine has usually known that outcome the week after the election. That matters because the Senate, now split 53 to 47 for Republicans, could hinge on close races in Alaska, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. Now the state that changed its rule: Ohio. A 2025 law says most absentee ballots must arrive by the time polls close. Before that, Ohio gave mail ballots four extra days to show up. Supporters say a firm deadline means faster, ... Critics worry about voters who still assume the old grace period applies.

items.excerpt: # Movie News From Around the World ¦ 1st November 2026. November 1, 2026 by bobwp ### Patrick Stewart’s final role, Cate Blanchett in Tokyo, Jailer 2 closes in on ₹800 crore & Nollywood’s ₦400 million October. Morning, all. A new month, and Sunday means our weekly lap of the world’s other film industries, but first, more on the loss of Sir Patrick Stewart. I’ll cover the confirmed weekend box office numbers in tomorrow’s post. Patrick Stewart’s farewell performance: Marvel Studios has confirmed that Avengers: Doomsday, which opens on 18 December, will be Sir Patrick Stewart’s final onscreen performance, which ends a 26-year run as Professor Xavier. It means he won’t appear in the already-filmed content for Avengers: Secret Wars. He appears opposite Sir Ian McKellen’s Magneto, and the pair have already appeared together in the trailers. McKellen’s tribute, in which he said Stewart wore his heart on his sleeve and was a man to rely on, to admire and, in his case, to love, ended by noting that Stewart’s farewell performance in Avengers: Doomsday is yet to be seen. McKellen recalled that when Stewart first told him about a Star Trek offer, he urged him to think of his stage career, which is advice that Stewart, happily for the rest of us, ignored. McKellen also officiated at Stewart’s 2013 wedding. Hugh Jackman, who played Wolverine opposite Stewart’s Professor X, called him one of the greats of stage and screen, and Rebecca Romijn thanked him as a fellow mutant and a fellow member of Starfleet. The Far East: Cate Blanchett in Tokyo: At the Tokyo International Film Festival on Friday, the first five short films made through Cate Blanchett’s Displacement Film Fund were screened, with Blanchett joined for a Q&A by the fund’s directors Shahrbanoo Sadat and Mohammad Rasoulof, and with help from Perfect Days actor Kōji Yakusho. Sadat’s feature No Good Men was also at the London Film Festival this month. The festival runs until 4 November. Tamil cinema: Jailer 2 closes in on ₹800 crore: Rajinikanth’s Jailer 2 stands at ₹776.95 crore (about $81 million) worldwide and ₹435.4 crore net (about $45 million) in India after 16 days, according to Sacnilk, and it’s closing in on the ₹800 crore milestone. Its ₹509.45 crore gross in India is within ₹10 crore of the all-time Tamil record in India, held by 2.0. I’ll bring you the full third-weekend numbers tomorrow. Nollywood’s ₦400 million October: In Nigeria, faith-based hit Agbara Nla: The Return topped the chart for a fourth weekend with ₦32.8 million (about $25,000) from 5,477 admissions over 23–25 October, taking it to ₦408.3 million (about $307,000), which makes it the first October release ever to pass ₦400 million. By Thursday its total had reached ₦422.7 million (about $318,000). Among the new releases, the campus drama Tele x Zikora, directed by Adenike Adebayo-Esho, had the biggest opening with ₦26.9 million (about $20,000), while Clayface opened fourth with ₦16.8 million (about $13,000). Fusion Intelligence expects 2026 to pass the whole of 2025’s Nigerian box office total early this month, helped by higher ticket prices. Birthdays: Toni Collette, star of The Sixth Sense and Hereditary, turns 54 today, and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan of Devdas turns 53. Also celebrating is Rob Riggle (56), who stars in Christmas at the Kringles, which opened in US cinemas on Friday.

The show, running for three weeks at New York City Center, features a new cast of Latino artists. Mendizábal emphasizes the importance of showcasing Latino communities, especially now. Miranda, who starred in the original production, reflects on the musical's enduring relevance. The revival comes amid immigration tensions, highlighting themes of gentrification and community. New and old cast members say the musical remains a celebration of the Latino immigrant experience, with its messages resonating strongly today. Heidi Klum reveals Halloween costume as ... Houdini’s centennial spotlight: A newly published essay and a fresh fight over when and how he died NEW YORK (AP) — Harry Houdini, a century after his death, continues to captivate. A rare essay by the escape artist has been published, shedding light on his early influences. A recent book revisits questions about the cause and date of his death. Houdini, born Erik Weisz, became an international celebrity known for his escape acts. His mysterious death on Halloween 1926 remains debated, with new theories challenging the official cause. Centennial events this weekend include a "Grand Houdini Centenarium" in Budapest, an auction in Hollywood, and seances in Chicago and Maryland. Despite the intrigue, experts say his legacy endures through his remarkable life. Scott Clifton and Tamara Tunie earn lead acting Daytime Emmys. 'General Hospital' wins again LOS ANGELES (AP) — Scott Clifton of “The Bold and the Beautiful” and Tamara Tunie of “Beyond the Gates” have won lead acting honors at the Daytime Emmy Awards. It's Clifton's second career trophy in the lead category. Tunie made her return to the soap opera genre after 17 years away. “General Hospital” won its record 19th trophy overall as outstanding drama and sixth in a row. Roger Howarth and Beth Maitland of “The Young and the Restless” swept the supporting acting categories. Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, lost in the lifestyle program category for her former Netflix show “With Love, Meghan.” Margaret Qualley, Jack Antonoff file for divorce after 3 years of marriage NEW YORK (AP) — Actor Margaret Qualley and Grammy winner Jack Antonoff have filed for divorce after three years of marriage. Court records show the case was filed Friday in Kings County Supreme Court in New York as an uncontested matrimonial action. Qualley is listed as the plaintiff, and Antonoff as the defendant. The couple separated in July. Qualley, 32, is known for films like “The Substance” and “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.” Antonoff, 42, is a 14-time Grammy-winning songwriter and producer. The couple began dating in 2021 and married in August 2023. An introspective Kirk Franklin is no longer apologizing with 'I Am What I Am' album NEW YORK (AP) — Kirk Franklin is back with his new album, "I Am What I Am," out Friday. His 14th studio project and first double album, 14 tracks are divided between contemporary music and traditional, live-recorded gospel songs. Features include gospel royalty Karen Clark Sheard and star mainstream artists like Jelly Roll, Davido and GloRilla. “This Time," featuring GloRilla, hit No. 1 on Billboard’s hot gospel songs, extending Franklin's record to ten No. 1s on the chart.
